newsitem.title: UK: Shell delays shutdown of Brent Bravo field.
newsitem.headline: Shell delays shutdown of Brent Bravo field.

text.p: A maintenance shutdown scheduled at the Brent Bravo field for the first week of June has been postponed, a spokesman for Brent system operator Shell Exploration and Production (Shell Expro) said on Friday.
The maintenance at the 70,000 barrels per day (bpd) field will now take place in August.
"It's been postponed until August...We always say our maintenance schedules are subject to adjustment," the spokesman said.
Last month Shell Expro said it had cancelled a maintenance shutdown planned for June 22-28 at the 55,000 bpd Tern field, which also feeds the Brent system.
North Sea crude traders have speculated that shutdowns have been cancelled due to production problems in the Brent field system.
"There are always production fluctuations and as far as we're concerned things are normal at the moment," the spokesman said.
But he added that other fields, not operated by Shell Expro, also feed into the Brent system.

Brent system throughput includes crude production from 13 fields and several satellite wells piped to the Sullom Voe terminal in the Shetland Islands where it is blended with Ninian crude and exported as Brent Blend.
Shell Expro is a joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Exxon Corp.
